h1: Nectaron hops for pineapple and peach in a hazy IPA
title: Nectaron Hops for Pineapple in Hazy IPA | Craft Beer School
desc: Nectaron hops for hazy IPA: alpha and aroma, a 20 litre recipe with dry hop timing and how to keep pineapple and peach from fading in Indian heat.
teaser: Nectaron brings pineapple and peach to a hazy IPA. Keeping that fruit for more than a few weeks is the hard part.
standfirst: Nectaron is a New Zealand hop bred for tropical fruit, with pineapple, peach and passion fruit up front. It suits hazy IPAs well. Here is how to build one that tastes of Nectaron rather than of grass and oxidation.
sections:
Nectaron is a recent release from New Zealand, grown in the Nelson region at the top of the South Island, where most of the country's hops are farmed. It is sold as an aroma variety, so treat it that way.

Alpha acid is fairly high for an aroma hop, usually around 10 to 12%. The aroma is the reason to buy it: pineapple, peach, passion fruit and grapefruit. In a hazy IPA it reads as juicy and tropical rather than piney.
What makes a hazy IPA work

A hazy IPA, sometimes called New England IPA, is built around soft bitterness, a full body and a big late hop aroma. Typical numbers:

  • OG 1.060 to 1.070 for 6 to 7% ABV.
  • Bitterness low for an IPA, often 25 to 40 IBU.
  • Oats and wheat at 15 to 30% of the grist for body and haze.
  • Water with more chloride than sulphate for a softer mouthfeel.

The aroma comes almost entirely from whirlpool and dry hops. That is where Nectaron goes.
A 20 litre hazy IPA with Nectaron

Here is a recipe at about OG 1.064 and 30 IBU:

  • Pilsner or pale malt 4.6 kg (75%).
  • Flaked oats 0.92 kg (15%).
  • Wheat malt 0.61 kg (10%).
  • A small bittering charge at 60 minutes for about 10 IBU, or none.
  • Nectaron 60 g in a 20 minute whirlpool at 75 to 80 °C.
  • Nectaron 80 g dry hop on day two or three of fermentation.
  • Nectaron 80 g dry hop after fermentation, for three days.

That is about 8 g per litre of dry hop, at the lower end of many hazy IPA recipes. Start there. Use a low flocculating yeast at 18 to 20 °C.
The floor detail: oxygen kills hazy IPA

Hazy IPAs are notoriously sensitive to oxygen. A beer that tasted of fresh pineapple at packaging can turn dull, brown and cardboard-like within a few weeks if oxygen gets in. The hop compounds that make it juicy are the first to go.

At home, the worst moment is usually the second dry hop. Opening the fermenter lets air in. Use a dry hop port if you have one, or add the hops quickly and close the lid. Purge bottles or kegs with CO2 if you can. If you bottle, add priming sugar so the yeast has something to ferment and use up some of the oxygen. Drink the beer within a month or two.
Why the first dry hop goes in early

Adding hops during active fermentation exposes them to working yeast. Yeast can transform some hop compounds into new aroma compounds, a process brewers call biotransformation. The result tends to be juicier and fruitier than the same hops added after fermentation.

Early dry hopping also uses the CO2 being produced to carry away some of the oxygen the hops bring in. The second dry hop, after fermentation, adds fresher top notes. Using both gives you depth and lift.
Mash and water for a soft body

The body of a hazy IPA comes from the mash and the adjuncts. Mash at 66 to 67 °C to keep some dextrins. Oats bring beta-glucans and proteins that add silkiness and help hold the haze, but they also make lautering slower. Rice hulls at around 3 to 5% of the grist weight help a homebrew mash drain.

For water, many brewers aim for chloride at roughly twice the sulphate. That rounds the bitterness and suits pineapple and peach better than a sharp, sulphate-heavy profile. Start from soft or RO water so you know what you are building on.

Nectaron works alone, but blends can add depth:

  • With Sultana to double up on pineapple.
  • With Lotus for orange and a creamy vanilla edge.
  • With Citra or Mosaic for a more familiar tropical base.

Keep Nectaron at half or more of the late hop weight if you want it to lead.

Hops grown on the other side of the world have a long journey to a homebrewer in Pune or Bengaluru. Buy from suppliers who keep stock frozen and ship with ice packs in the hot months. Check the harvest year. Freeze the pack the day it arrives.

Then think about the finished beer. A hazy IPA left in a warm room for two weeks fades faster than one kept cold. Keep packaged beer in the fridge from the start. Heat speeds up every reaction that turns pineapple into stale fruit.

Haze stability, hop aroma retention and oxidation all come down to chemistry: proteins and polyphenols, hop oils and yeast, oxygen and time. A brewer who understands those mechanisms can predict how a beer will taste in six weeks, not only on packaging day. That prediction is the part a recipe cannot teach.
faqs: Pineapple, peach, passion fruit and grapefruit. It reads as juicy and tropical rather than piney.
How much Nectaron should I use in a hazy IPA?
Around 8 g per litre of dry hop split across two additions is a reasonable start for a 20 litre batch, plus a whirlpool addition.
Why does my hazy IPA turn brown?
Usually oxygen. Hop compounds and malt oxidise quickly, darkening the beer and dulling the aroma. Limit air exposure during dry hopping and packaging.
